title: 'Flock Flocked up'

reading.body:
This is a false alert from an automated license plate reader being treated as established fact in the field. The camera's image matched a Chevy Malibu, but the alert was attached to a red Dodge Ram pickup, so the mismatch was present in the alert itself. The failure sits at the handoff between the system and the officers who act on it, where a machine-generated flag arrived with the authority of a verified report and was not checked against the vehicle in front of them.

Catching it would have required comparing the alerted vehicle's make and model against the truck before the stop escalated, or a rule that an alert alone does not justify a stop. Neither happened. The stop proceeded on the alert, and the plate information was found to be wrong only afterward.

What is not established is where the error originated, whether in the camera's reading or in the plate data behind it. The department's investigation found no wrongdoing in the use of the K9, and the charges were dropped according to the man's lawyer. A wrong alert is not by itself evidence of intent or of a defect.

reports.title: Body cam of TPD officers releasing K-9 on man during traffic stop
Man speaks out after police release K-9 on him during traffic stop: 'Traumatized'
TPD investigation finds no wrongdoing in use of K-9 on man during traffic stop
Charges dropped against man Toledo Police released K-9 on during traffic stop, lawyer says

summary:
New body camera video released Monday shows Toledo police using a K9 on a man during a traffic stop. The driver, Brandon Upchurch, was stopped after an officer got a FLOCK camera alert about a stolen license plate. The report says the alert was wrong. The camera image matched a Chevy Malibu but appeared on a red Dodge Ram pickup. Officers stopped the truck leaving a carryout, drew guns, and told Upchurch to get out. He got out with his hands up and asked why he was stopped. Officers told him to turn around and lie down. He walked into the grass, and the K9 handler moved closer with the dog.

Upchurch was arrested and charged with resisting arrest and obstruction. Officers later learned the plate information was wrong and the truck did not have the stolen plate. Medical attention was given at the scene. Police said they thought Upchurch might flee and did not know if he or the passenger had weapons. Multiple Toledo officers were under investigation after the K9 release.
